name: Abed-nego
source_summary: One of Daniel's three Judean companions, given a Babylonian name in exile, who refused to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and was miraculously preserved unharmed in a fiery furnace.
family_friendly_summary: Abednego, whose Hebrew name was Azariah, was one of Daniel's three close friends who were taken from Judah to Babylon and trained to serve in the king's court. When King Nebuchadnezzar set up a huge golden statue and commanded everyone to bow down and worship it, Abednego and his two friends refused, because they would only worship the one true God. Furious, the king had them thrown into a blazing furnace, heated so hot that the soldiers who threw them in were killed by the heat. But God protected Abednego and his friends completely -- they walked around unharmed inside the flames, and witnesses even saw a fourth figure with them. When they came out, not even their clothes smelled of smoke. Nebuchadnezzar was amazed and honored their God.
adult_story: Abednego was the Babylonian name given to Azariah, one of the young Judean nobles taken to Babylon with Daniel and trained for royal service (Daniel 1:6-7). Along with Shadrach and Meshach, he was later promoted to administer the province of Babylon at Daniel's request (2:49). When King Nebuchadnezzar erected a ninety-foot golden image and commanded all officials to bow and worship it at the sound of music, Abednego, Shadrach, and Meshach refused, since bowing to an idol would violate their exclusive worship of the LORD (3:1-12). Reported to the furious king, they answered him with remarkable resolve: "our God whom we serve is able to deliver us... but even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we are not going to serve your gods" (3:16-18) -- faith that did not depend on the outcome. Nebuchadnezzar had the furnace heated seven times hotter and had them bound and thrown in, so hot that the soldiers who threw them in were killed by the flames (3:19-23). Yet the king, watching, saw four men walking unbound and unharmed in the fire, the fourth appearing "like a son of the gods" (3:24-25). Abednego and his companions emerged without so much as the smell of smoke on them, and Nebuchadnezzar publicly praised their God and promoted them further (3:26-30) -- one of Scripture's most vivid demonstrations that God can deliver His faithful even from certain death, and is worthy of worship whether He does or not.
christ_connections: Abednego's resolve to obey God rather than an earthly decree, whatever the cost, models the faith Hebrews 11 commends -- trusting God's power to deliver while submitting to His will even if He does not.

Many readers have seen the unharmed fourth figure in the furnace, described as like "a son of the gods," as a preincarnate appearance of Christ standing with His faithful people in the fire -- Scripture does not name him, so this remains a traditional reading rather than a stated fact.
devotionals: Abednego trusted God to save him, but said he'd stay faithful even if God didn't. May we hold that same trust, whatever happens to us.
A fourth figure stood with them in the fire, unharmed. God is just as close to us in our hardest moments.
